revision: H1: In the 904-line held-out rice candidate pool, lines ranked highest by the rice_gs Ridge genomic prediction (E1) are enriched for membership in the top quartile of measured GRWT100. A closed-loop design that (a) predicts all 904 lines, (b) spends the 30-query phenotyping budget mostly on the top predicted tail with a small calibration spread sample, and (c) re-ranks by measured values after each round, will identify 10 lines with high probability of being in the measured high-grain-weight quartile. Testable: Spearman(measured, predicted) > 0 on the sampled lines, and the top predicted tail shows measurable quartile enrichment versus the 25% base rate.
reason: Initial hypothesis for the rice closed-loop selection task; model card reports held-out Spearman ~0.454 and top-20 quartile hit 1.00, which I will verify with real oracle measurements rather than assume.

plan.design: Round 1: query oracle for 10 lines at predicted ranks 1-10 plus 2 calibration lines (predicted-median rank ~452 and low tail rank ~890). Round 2: query lines at predicted ranks 11-20 (re-ranked and re-examined after Round 1). Round 3: query lines at predicted ranks 21-28 to complete the 30-query budget. After each round compute Spearman(predicted, measured) and measured-value percentile position; revise the candidate ranking; final top-10 chosen by measured GRWT100 among the phenotyped set, with calibrated predictions used only for any unphenotyped tie-break.
controls: Same trait (GRWT100), same candidate pool (904 held-out lines), identical model weights for every round

all ranking decisions use the same scoring rule so rounds are comparable. The 4 calibration lines spanning predicted range are held fixed so calibration slope/residual are estimated on a non-truncated sample.
plan.observation_metric: Measured GRWT100 (g per 100 grains) per line from the hidden oracle (E3); Spearman rank correlation between E1 predicted and E3 measured; number of final-10 lines whose measured value exceeds the estimated 75th percentile of the pool.
plan.refutation_condition: Hypothesis is refuted if Spearman(measured, predicted) <= 0 on the 30 sampled lines (predictions carry no rank signal), or if the top predicted tail shows no quartile enrichment (hit rate statistically indistinguishable from the 25% base rate), in which case a random or prediction-free selection would be equally defensible.

revision: H1 (confirmed with caveat): The rice_gs top-predicted tail is genuinely enriched for high measured GRWT100 (24/30 phenotyped lines above the estimated ~2.76 g quartile threshold). However, single-line genomic predictions are noisy (sigma~0.59 g) and can badly miss (two top-30 predicted lines measured only 2.0-2.1 g). Therefore the defensible final top-10 is the set of phenotyped lines with the highest E3 measured values (3.4-5.0 g), using E1 only to break the 3.4 g tie, not a pure prediction-based ranking.
reason: Confirmed by three rounds of real E3 measurements: Spearman(pred,measured)=0.63 with 24/30 phenotyped lines above the estimated quartile threshold (~2.76 g) versus a 25% base rate. Caveat added: residual noise is large (sigma~0.59 g) and individual predictions are not reliable without phenotyping, so the final ranking is measurement-driven.
